text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Indian External Affairs Minister I.K. Gujral made it clear he did not expect "dramatic results" from the forthcoming foreign secretary-level talks but at the same time said he would be happy if they paved the way for India and Pakistan "to learn to live as close friends and neighbours".

- The government's new economic reform package will reduce the number of public sector corporations from 120 to 50, cut import tariffs to 45 percent from 65 percent and personal and corporate tax to 36 and 38 percent respectively and broaden general sales tax to retail level.
- Three Egyptian nationals, entrenched in an Afghan refugee tent village and defying arrest, have killed one of their companions and a 12-year-old boy, a government official said.
- Turkish President Suleyman Demirel offered to initiate joint industrial ventures with Pakistan, including production of defence equipment.

- Five big banks have been asked to identify 25 percent of their branches which are loss-making or marginally profitable to enable a closure plan to be drawn up for presentation to a World Bank team by the State (centra) Bank of Pakistan. The World Bank is seeking a 40 percent reduction in manpower in the big banks.
- Iranian President Ali Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said Iran has proposals to lay a gas pipeline to Pakistan to be extended to India.
- The government has decided to divert funds amounting to four billion rupees to complete work on the Chashma Nuclear Power and the People's Steel Mills projects.
- Pakistan and Turkey have decided to revive the abandoned Islamabad-Peshawar motorway project.
- The state-run Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd plans to raise one billion rupees by floating commercial paper in the capital markets.

- Al-Meezan Investment bank with an initial paid-up capital of one billion rupees is being launched in Pakistan by the Pak-Kuwait Investment Company and the Islamic Investment Company of the Gulf, Bahrain.
- Supreme Court chief justice Sajjad Ali Shah has ordered police officers to explain why they had handcuffed three senior government officers on the orders of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif.
- The Islamic Taleban government in Afghanistan has released 37 members of Pakistani Anti-Narcotics Force who were arrested after they entered Afghanistan while chasing drug smugglers.
